back: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons (same proton number, different nucleon number).
The total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

front: Relative masses and charges of the proton, neutron and electron?
back: Proton: mass 1, charge +1. Neutron: mass 1, charge 0. Electron: mass 1/1836, charge −1.

front: How do you find the number of neutrons from isotope notation?
back: Neutrons $= A - Z$ (nucleon number minus proton number).

front: Why do isotopes have the same chemical properties?
back: Same number of protons → same number and arrangement of electrons; chemical reactions involve electrons.
notes: Mass-dependent physical properties (density, diffusion rate) differ.

front: What decides the size of deflection of a particle beam in an electric field?
back: The charge-to-mass ratio: a larger charge or a smaller mass gives a larger deflection. Direction: towards the oppositely charged plate.

front: How are electrons, protons and neutrons deflected between charged plates?
back: Electrons: strongly towards the positive plate. Protons: slightly towards the negative plate. Neutrons: not deflected.

front: Why does atomic radius decrease across a period?
back: Nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell (similar shielding), so outer electrons are pulled closer.
Cations are smaller than their atoms (fewer shells / fewer electrons for the same nuclear charge). Anions are larger (more electron repulsion, same nuclear charge).
